Source: https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/Think-Aloud_Protocol_of_Instagram_Feed_and_Fitspiration_Browsing_/21195811 (file "Feed Transcripts (concurrent & retrospective).docx"; Davies, Turner & Udell, University of Portsmouth, 2022)
Licence: CC BY 4.0
Description: Concurrent + retrospective think-aloud transcripts of ~18 female participants (pseudonyms) browsing their own Instagram feed for 5 minutes; "Image description:" lines are researcher annotations of the post on screen.

Feed Transcripts (concurrent & retrospective)
Participant 2
Feed – Concurrent
Image description: meme painting of skeleton with words above it.
Rose: So, immediately this has got my attention because it’s student problems – posts that I absolutely relate to and are the ones that I actually read. They always make me feel a little bit better, for instance this one ‘When you have to keep reading the same paragraph because you can’t focus’. I’ve done this so many times that at one point I started to question whether it’s a language issue or whether I’m just dumb. You can really see with the student problems that people sometimes comment and say that they do the same thing. So it kinda makes you feel like it’s not just you.
Image description: image of female comedian on stage.
Rose: This is one of my favourite stand-up comedians, her name is Iliza Shlesinger. She does stand up, she is really funny and she is somebody that I, again, relate to. But as you can see I never actually do any likes.
Image description: blank with lyrics changed in a way that is supposed to be amusing.
Rose: Again, student problems which literally made me laugh this morning. This is the song I was singing in the shower at my honeymoon when I was super drunk at 3 o’clock in the morning. So, it kinda made me laugh as well for that reason.
Image description: thin female with long hair decorating Christmas tree.
Rose: And then of course we have the typical beautiful picture of Christmas fantasy, I don’t know whose fantasy it is. Let’s face it every girl when she is decorating the Christmas tree has to do a full head of beautiful curls and face of make-up bows and tiny little shorts with no bra and really loose t-shirt. This is exactly how we dress up when getting ready to decorate [for] Christmas. This is the kind of picture that I absolutely hate, I’m not going to like it, I’m not going to do anything about it, it’s just so incredibly fake.
Image description: news story, two images split screen with click bait title above.
Rose: And, there is BuzzFeed, it depends on the story sometimes I look at it sometimes I don’t. This one is about celebrities, I don’t really care so I am just going to go browse.
Image description: new story, two images split screen with click bait title above.
Rose: I actually read this one I thought that was quite cute, it was about Jack Black who forgot he was in the holiday and his reactions towards it, so that was quite cute. So, sometimes if I found the actual article on here interesting I will go to find the actual article and read it.
Image description: meme with image of iPhone calculator.
Rose: And then again one of the little silly comics.
Image description: image of same female comedian with a caption next to it.
Rose: This is again one of Iliza’s silly comments. She got a little bit preachy recently so I don’t necessarily like that, that much.
Image description: new article about a film, with movie poster as image.
Rose: When there is too much text when I’m just browsing I’m not going to read it
Rose: BuzzFeed recently they have a lot of posts about ‘these are the best gifts’ or ‘you really need these items’, I’m like no ‘you’re just being sponsored I’m not going to watch this’.
Image description: magazine cover of man.
Rose: Oh, this is Queer Eye’s Jonathon, I really like him. He just keeps it real. But what I actually don’t like about him sometimes. And what a lot of the Queer Eye crew do, they’re being sponsored by a lot of things, so they do a lot of advertisements.
Image description: bowl of pasta.
Rose: Then you have the food. If it’s good or sounds interesting then maybe I will look into it more
Image description: political image with stats
Rose: I follow Bernie Sanders because he is great, I just hope he will win. So, hope he will win.
Image description: tweet about primary vote stats for American election.
Rose: And then, yeah that looks good because I was really hoping … it’s really good to see it but it’s really disappointing because you see that he is doing so so great but nothing really comes out of it afterwards.
Image description: new article
Rose: And then the New York Times. What I actually find annoying with the New York Times, because they do actually have really good pictures and articles, but you can only view maybe like 3 articles a month otherwise you have to have a subscription.
Image description: image of scenery
Rose: Then national geographic, they actually have really interesting pictures. As you can see, what they do, they do a little description so you can follow up if you are interestest in the story.
Image description: image of celebrity on chat show couch with a text caption.
Rose: Um, the Ellen Show
Rose: Again, national geographic
Image description: image of cultural building at night.
Rose: I think the photos they have to be really striking as well, for me to engage.
Image description: Ellen Show post with the host and female celebrity.
Rose: Yep, I love Jenifer Aniston.
Rose: Iliza again, Bernie Sanders
Feed – Retrospective
R: Where there any posts that really stood out to you?
Rose: Um, not really. I know it’s funny but not really. I think for a photo to be really memorable or to stand out it really has to has to hit somewhere close, something that you really relate to.
R: Were there any posts that made you feel anything in particular?
Rose: No, because I think that I specifically follow stuff that I know won’t put me in a bad mood. So, I font necessarily follow celebrities. The only celebrities that I do follow are like Jenifer Aniston or Iliza Shlesinger or Ellen, people that I know won’t be posting half naked pictures of themselves. I make conscious decisions not to follow certain people.
R: Why is that?
Rose: Because I know they will be posting pictures of living a fantasy life and I won’t be able to relate to that and it will just annoy me.
R: I noticed that you said that memes tended to make you feel a bit better, could you tell me a bit more about that?
Rose: I think what it is, is because we all have our little quirks and we think we are the only one that has them – the little things that annoy us or that we go through so when we see a little funny joke about it on Instagram it’s so relatable. I think that is why I signed up to Twitter because there is a lot of that academic stuff going around that makes you feel like you’re not alone in how you’re feeling with uni work. You are not the only one who has to read the paragraph three times, say. So, it’s just little things like that that tell you it’s normal.
R: I noticed that you also said for one of the posts that if there is too much text you’d probably flick past it…
Rose: Unless, it’s an interesting picture. I think there is literally seconds to get one’s attention. The picture it has to be something that I can relate to for me to actually read what it’s about. It has to hook my attention for me to read what it’s about. There was one post were the title was like four lines and there was writing on the picture was more writing on the bottom, that’s too much I’m not going to read that. Unless it’s directly related to me.
R: You also mentioned sponsors, can you tell me a bit more about your reactions to them?
Rose: They are so incredibly frustrating. The most ridiculous one that I’ve seen recently was Johnathon form Queer Eye he was sponsored by toilet paper and he was saying he always packs one just in case when he travels, yeah that’s exactly what I do I always have a toilet paper in my carry-on then of course I leave it on my bed, just like I don’t want to know why you have toilet paper on your bed. Yes, we all use toilet paper, but do you really have your favourite brand that you always buy. So, I just find things that that a little bit annoying and it makes the characters [sponsored people] a little bit more, I find them less credible. It makes me question their honesty, as they use a lot of products in their TV show was well so how do I know when they aren’t being sponsored. Even if I see a pretty picture when I realise it is sponsored I will just pay it no attention and skip it.
Participant 3
Feed – Concurrent
Post description: video close up on the face of a women, wearing lots of makeup and focusing on her eyelashes.
Hattie: I’ve um, zoomed in on this girl’s eyelashes. Her lips look really big as well. So, that’s caught my attention. And she’s got really high cheek bones, that has also caught my attention.
Post description: women stood posing in front of clothes stand.
Hattie: There is also a picture of a girl, who I know from school, who’s got her own business. So, I am just like being nosy. [Looking] At what type of clothes, she is selling and stuff. And now I’ve gone to her profile just to have a quick look.
Post description: collection of three images that are close up pictures of a woman’s eyes with big long eyelashes.
Hattie: There’s another ad of, um, false eyelashes that have caught my attention again.
Post description: multiple images of a women and a group of friends.
Hattie: There’s a picture of, well a couple of pictures of this girl that I used to go to school with ages ago. And I’m just looking at her and her other girl-friends. And the clothes they’re wearing.
Post description: two pictures of a women and man at a party.
Hattie: In this picture here, there seems to be like a lot going on. Like, the pres in this picture look more exciting than the ones I have at uni (laughter).
Post description: advert of before and after cosmetic surgery images of a woman’s face.
Hattie: I keep seeing this ad, as well pop up. Of this girl who has had like her face redone.
Post description: two selfies of a woman smiling.
Hattie: Here’s a picture of a girl, who knew my ex (laughter), every time I see her I get so frustrated. I don’t know why I still follow her, it’s just being nosy I guess.
Post description: on profile of woman, contains lots of posed images. Different images viewed: selfies, images with other people in, quote-based images, videos.
Hattie: This account, um, is one of my friends and she’s like, she um, does like her own Depop thing but she’s all really like, I don’t know. She’s all about positivity and stuff as well. So, I think it’s like when I see her posts and stuff I feel like it, kinda makes me feel better because she documents everything she goes through as well. So, like, it makes me feel better that oh like if I’m having a bad day, other people are [too].
Post description: two images of a women at a cocktail bar, one of her posing and one of her pouring a cocktail into her glass.
Hattie: This story here is a bit annoying because these are people that I go to uni with and I don’t understand how they’ve got money to be going to the Alchemist.
Post description: Images of a woman’s eyes, she has big long eyelashes.
Hattie: There’s more ads again for the eyelashes.
Feed – Retrospective
R: Were there any posts that really stood out to you?
Hattie: Um, not really. They’re all kinda the same. Apart from that one, um, of people having pictures at pres. That kinda stood out a bit. Just because, I think like when I pre here at uni and stuff it’s a bit like ‘ah other people are having more fun, like, is this a bit flat’, you know? Like, people having [more] fun elsewhere. I feel like, is it me? Do you know what I mean? Am I not like the life and soul?
R: Um, so, were there any posts that made you feel anything in particular?
Hattie: Um, that one of that girl who knew my ex. That one, like, yeah it kinda left a bit of a bitter taste. So, like, I don’t know why I still follow her, but it’s just like that part of you. You know when you’re like, you just don’t need to do that, but I do so I don’t know. [I] do it to myself.
R: Okay, so I noticed that you have quite a lot of eyelashes come up…
Hattie: … Yeah.
R: … can you tell me a bit more about that?
Hattie: Um, recently … well I used to get extensions. And like when I had them I really liked them. But they damaged my eyelashes afterwards, and yeah kinda. But I really want to get them again, so I’ve been looking and my phone obviously, probably knows … remembered that and is giving me all the ads. But yeah, I like the way I look with eyelashes. Someone once told me ‘oh, you’ve got nice eyes’, so that’s really stuck in my head and so now I want to like do everything to draw attention to them I guess. So, yeah, I’m just interested in eyelashes and stuff.
R: So, do you find that adverts are quite targeted?
Hattie: Yeah, massively. So, like if I look at one thing one day I’ll get like 20 ads, for the next week, of it. If that makes sense? So, like, I don’t know.
R: Hmm, do you like this or do you not like this, or do you not have an opinion?
Hattie: Yeah, no. I don’t really have an issue with it. It’s just eyelashes. If it was something else I guess, more like body related rather than just like eyelashes I guess it would play a bit more of a role like on my mental health, or like something like that. But yeah, for the moment it’s fine.
R: So, you also mentioned something about one of your friends having quite a positive account.
Hattie: Yeah.
R: So, can you tell me a bit more about why that is?
Hattie: Um, so, she graduated uni and she wanted to stay where she lived at uni um she’s like finding it quite hard struggling. Um and like I follow her to give her support and stuff and because she’s like trying to do this business on Depop and stuff and like she wants to like make it, so yeah. I follow her because I want to give her support. I want to see what she’s up to and like keep in touch with my friend for one, and also, yeah just be there for her I guess.

Feed – Retrospective
R: Were there any posts that really stood out to you?
Jessica: Um, the ones that weren’t like BuzzFeed or uberfacts, any of my friends’ ones, I guess, stood out because I ‘liked’ them or had already ‘liked’ them.
R: So why do you think it is that you gravitate a bit more towards those?
Jessica: I guess because I am interested in finding out what other people are doing, especially if they are not at the uni the majority of my friends from home I’m still interested in what their uni life is like. That kind of thing.
R: So, were there any posts that made you feel anything in particular?
Jessica: Um, yeah there were some. One of my friends from here was posting a picture from the gym and then obviously I was like ‘oh I don’t look like that’ so that was, yeah. Stuff like that I see quite a lot, different body types and stuff.
R: Why do you think that is?
Jessica: I guess, because obviously I said about social media effects my body image but also like especially if they are my friends and I personally think they look better than me that affects me even more because I’m like in a close environment with them so it means that if they can do it I can do it. That probably affects me more than other stuff.
R: Okay, so, I noticed that you said you had quite a few targeted adverts?
Jessica: Yeah.
R: And they were fashion mainly?
Jessica: Yeah, clothes and stuff.
R: So, what do you think about this?
Jessica: Um, I guess it’s helpful in a way. Yeah it is a bit weird if they know where you shop or if it’s just like general adverts. It doesn’t bother me massively because if it’s stuff that I normally look at, which most of it was. Then I guess it’s just like know what deals are there and stuff.
R: Do you find that you pay attention to adverts when you see them?
Jessica: Not normally, unless it’s something that I would normally use. So, H&M and Missguided I might have a quick look at to see if, like what’s it saying really. So, yeah.
R: And then, so I also noticed you had a lot of BuzzFeed…
Jessica: Yeah (laughter).
R: …do you think you use Instagram as also a source of information?
Jessica: Um, yeah sometimes. BuzzFeed not the most credible thing, I don’t really watch BuzzFeed on YouTube anymore either, but I do still follow it so I guess if there is a news story I would probably have a look.

Megan: She posts a lot.
Megan: I don’t really stay long on a person’s picture unless I know them or if something catches my eye.
Image description: couple together in a bath.
Megan: Um, there’s a picture of a couple which makes me miss my boyfriend. And it then makes me kind of envious or jealous of their relationship because I kind of compare it to my own, because I see that they post a lot.
Image description: 4 images of the same woman in a pub setting.
Megan: ‘gram pictures of people I know and who I was friends with kind of are the posts that I always compare me and my own life to theirs and what they are getting up to.
Megan: I like most of the pictures on my timeline out of habit.
Megan: I kind of flick between looking at the timeline and looking at the stories, if I get bored of one or the other.
Image description: woman in selfie.
Megan: there’s a few people that I follow, who I know that I always get… like I always compare myself to them so I know I should just probably unfollow them, but for some reason I don’t.
Image description: celebrity woman’s story first image of presents under the Christmas tree.
Megan: If I person has a really long story then often I will skip past it.
Image description: image with text aimed at encouraging people to vote.
Megan: There’s a lot of stuff about like voting and stuff today, so I think that’s making me feel better about the election. I am hoping that people vote labour.
Image description: meme about behaviours considered characteristic of one of the star signs.
Megan: I follow a lot of astrology pages, I always take a while to look at what they post. Especially if it is to do with a sign of me or someone I know, and I always relate back to them.
Feed – Retrospective
R: Were there any posts that stood out to you?
Megan: Yeah, I think the ones that were more eye catching. Ones with nice colours, I think I pay more attention to those. The ones with nice aesthetic.
R: what type of posts are those?
Megan: Um, I think, like the film and photography ones, yeah that have eye-catching colours. I notice them more on my feed.
R: Okay, so were there any posts that made you feel anything in particular?
Megan: Yeah, the one of the person and her boyfriend. It made me think of my relationship and compare my relationship to theirs. How they seem and how I am with my boyfriend. And the one of one of my friend, I compared myself there as well, how I look to how she looks in the post.
R: Where these negative or positive feelings?
Megan: negative, their lives looked better than mine.
R: So, you said that you thought that you could beneficially unfollow certain people, could you tell me a bit more about that please?
Megan: Yeah so, I think I should unfollow people who I compare myself to because I don’t really get anything from it so there is no point.
R: to clarify, is the comparison negative or positive.
Megan: Definitely negative, it makes me feel worse about myself.
R: In what way is that?
Megan: If they look more attractive than I do in a post or in the picture that I post, then I feel worse about my appearance. Um, and then if they look like they are having more fun in their relationship then it makes me feel that mine isn’t as good as theirs.

Feed – Concurrent

Ellen: So, I’ve come across Compose which is like a gym. They get all of their models and stuff from Instagram, like they’ve asked me to do it before. They post peoples’ home workouts that they do at home and stuff. So, it’s just a build your plan advertisement, but yeah, it’s something that they’ve asked me to do before.
Image description: video advertisement of a festival.

Ellen: It’s just my friend that I’d normal like and comment on that because she is a close friend of mine. It’s a mirror selfie.

Ellen: It’s a make-up look, I follow a lot of things from there. She’s doing like a Valentines look which is nice it’s just I like watching videos like this.
Image description: words on a plain background with a feminist type theme.
Ellen: This is a quote that is like a motivational account they post a lot of things, it says ‘to the women called aggressive keep being assertive, to the women called bossy keep on leading’ etc, it’s a different mindset…
Image description: motivational words written on a bit of paper.
Ellen: … it’s the same as this one the Mayfair group which is just a lot of nice positive things. It says ‘Mayfair reminder: Speak as if it has already happened and it will.’ Yeah, that’s just a manifestation thing.
Image description: image of woman in underwear laying on a bed.
Ellen: This lounge underwear it’s just a lot of nice… this is probably the ideal body type. A lot of those posts. Which at the moment it’s motivational because I am going to the gym.
Image description: image of woman in mirror sat on a stool posed.
Ellen: Ellie Darby, she posts a lot of fashion things, I think all of her outfits are unreal. I get a lot of what she wears from that, I don’t copy it, but I get a lot of ideas from her.
Feed – Retrospective
R: Were there any posts that really stood out to you?
Ellen: I think the compose one, that was the home workouts one because I hadn’t seen it in a while and I was like ‘oh my god’ because I got back into working out and I had completely forgotten about it. I think it’s because it related to me more because I remember them asking me to do it and then I got really interested in it. And then probably the lounge, I don’t know if it was just because we were talking about it [the ideal body type]. And my friend that I was going to comment on, I think it was because it was a familiar face from the other ones.
R: Do you find that you gravitate more towards the familiar ones?
Ellen: Yeah definitely. Things that I’m not as familiar with, I tend to just skip past.
R: So, were there any posts that made you feel anything in particular?
Ellen: Um, not really. The lounge one I was thinking ‘should I keep following them, is it healthy to keep following them?’ I don’t think that it’s as bad as it was anymore, but it is very much like wishful thinking with them. Like, adverts and seeing like models and stuff and that’s when it’s like ‘oh I wish’… it’s not that it’s as deep as that it’s just I don’t know if it should be on my timeline as much as it is.
R: Because it makes you feel a bit negative sometimes?
Ellen: Yeah.
R: What is the difference between posts that you do like or posts that you maybe, like less?
Ellen: The posts that I’m interested in or enjoy are the ones from my friends I’m curious about what they’ve posted or something. I skip everything else if I don’t really know them or I’m not interested.
R: So, you feel that’s what separates out?
Ellen: Yeah, and like even if I don’t know some of the girls but I like their outfit then I’ll stop at that to see what it is. But I normally tend to skip out people that I’m not as close with. I try not to follow people that I’m not as close with but, I don’t know how but, you just sort of end up following people that you have heard of but you aren’t close with them. I try and every so often go through who I follow and like ‘do I need that? Is that impacting me that much?’ and like I try and do that but I always forget.
R: So, you said something about the advert, was it the lounge wear advert?
Ellen: Yeah.
R: Is that an account you follow or?
Ellen: Yeah, I think I do follow them because I think I’ve bought things from there before. Yeah, I had like two of them come up. I think I shouldn’t follow them because they are like model type, but it is also the body type that I like. But it’s probably not the healthiest way, because I don’t know, they’re really, not even just body type they’re really stunning girls so it’s like, not a bad thing. I don’t know, I end up buying loads of stuff from there because I think it looks really nice and it looks nice on her
R: You also mentioned something about the home workouts, can you tell me a bit more about this?
Ellen: They make me feel a bit better about my body because they are more genuine. I can trust it more because it’s real people, people that I know I can see effects from that, it’s a genuine change in their bodies.

Feed – Retrospective
R: So, did any of those posts stand out to you?

And there is a girl that I follow and she wears like one white contact [lens] and one black contact and she wears like really high up eyebrows which is really cool and she looks really goth and I really like that. They probably stood out to me the most, and probably the fact that the girl I went to 6th form with she looks so different on Instagram - she doesn’t look like that in real-life either, she’s a bit fat and her make-up is cakey.
R: Why do you think those posts in particular?
Zoe: I think maybe the photography because it’s quite nice to look at, it’s quite nicely done and it’s quite artsy. I like the aesthetical look of like the goth stuff, I think that is quite cool, but you can tell it is edited a lot, which means it’s not really a full kind of reality. I like looking at the tattoo ones because it’s either the tattoo artist that I follow or the ones that have done my tattoos, like what they are up to and stuff which is interesting for me because if I want more tattoos I will go all the way back home to get them done because I like them.
R: Where there any posts that made you feel anything in particular?
Zoe: The photography ones make me feel quite calm because they are quite scenic and nice.
R: I noticed that you said about the photography guy and how he never posts selfies…
Zoe: Yeah, he never does he just posts his photography stuff which is quite nice.
R: So, are selfies quite common on your feed then?
Zoe: Yeah, there are a lot of them on my feed and stuff and I don’t really follow as much photography as I want to and also cat and dog pics. But I don’t follow as much which is upsetting because I think maybe my life would be a bit happier if I had more cat and dog pics in my life.
R: So, do you think it is better for you to see more like cat and dog pics than it is for you to see selfies?
Zoe: Yeah, I think you can get consumed with seeing everyone’s selfies because I think you start becoming obsessive about looks. Whereas I think if you have a nice mixture… you know what you are going to get on my timeline because people post the same sort of things, so when something comes up that is a bit different it’s like ‘oh that’s nice’.
R: You said you saw a no make-up selfie, and you said that was quite good, why was that?
Zoe: Because I think a lot of the people I follow on Instagram do lots of really complex make-up looks, they blur out their face, have a ring light for selfies and stuff. It’s a whole like professional thing. So, it was nice to see a mirror selfie where she had no make-up on because she normally wears quite a lot, she looked natural so that was a refreshing difference I think.
R: When you say refreshing, do you think that most people aren’t like this?
Zoe: Yeah, I think it isn’t normalised to post no make-up selfies. I don’t wear make-up a lot and sometimes I think I look really good without it and sometimes I think I look like a crack head. I think it helps to normalise no make-up in everyday life if you are posting no make-up selfies or like if you follow more boys on Instagram as well that are like boy boys who don’t care about taking selfies – I came across one who now looks like a middle aged dad and his photos are so funny because he just takes the most horrendous photos and they just aren’t like the selfies you see from influencer girls and I just think it’s quite funny.

Mia: Not really, no. I don’t think so. There was that one account that I clicked on and she had her boobs done, made bigger, and then she got really ill and started getting really bloated. I follow her because she is a fitness influencer kind of thing, and she got her boobs taken out and she’s been trying to lose weight. She was going to the gym all day every day for like weeks and she got her boobs done and then taken out because she had like breast-plant illness, and when they were out she literally got back to normal just like that.
R: Did any of them make you feel anything in particular?
Mia: Some of them were relatable, like memes and stuff, so they are quite funny.
R: So, you mentioned surgery and you’ve mentioned the boob job thing, at one point you point out that she had obviously had surgery – how does that make you feel when you are looking at the picture?
Mia: I don’t know, I think that was a picture of Holly from Jordie Shore and I know they have all had surgery, like they’ve had something called BBL which is a Brazilian Bum Lift, you get the fat taken out of other places and put in your bum. Because of them I follow their plastic surgeon, it sounds so bad, but yeah, I know who has done their surgery and stuff and I follow that person. Sometime I look at it and I am like ‘ew no’, like I wouldn’t want do that but sometimes I look at it and think ‘I could get that done’. But then I have no money, so.
R: Do you think it normalises it a bit then?
Mia: Yeah.
R: Would you say that seeing it makes you more or less likely to get it, or doesn’t it affect you?
Mia: I think it makes me more likely to get it. I think it’s kind of a thing as well because they are openly talking about it which kind of removes the stigma of it. Before, 10 years ago, if you had surgery everyone would be shocked. But now so many people have it and so many people are posting about it.
R: So, there was also one where you mentioned a weight loss picture, what sort of picture was that?
Mia: That was on the same persons page that had her boobs taken out. Because she is a fitness influencer and has fitness plans, someone had done her plan and lost loads of weight in 12-weeks. It was like a before and after photo.
R: How do you think that affects you, to see those?
Mia: I think before and after photos make me think if she can do it I can do, and then it will motivate me for like 2-minutes. I think before and after photos are more of a positive rather than a negative.

Feed – Retrospective
R: Where there any posts that really stood out to you?
Taylor: A couple: hair related post.
R: Can you tell me a bit about those and why they stood out?
Taylor: Like there was a hair dying video, I didn’t watch all of it, but there was a couple of posts about really cool hair colours and they just stood out because I like dying my hair. It’s just what I am into, so.
R: Anything else that stood out to you in particular?
Taylor: There was a couple that used the same filter over and over, and it’s a bit like, very in your face, I have seen this picture like three times over now. It’s just people using the same filter.
R: Which filter?
Taylor: The Snapchat one with the hearts [lips] here [indicates to cheeks and nose area]. I saw it twice in the space of like two posts, it’s a bit unoriginal.
R: Why do you think people choose to use it?
Taylor: They think it makes them look cute. And they think it makes them look skinny in the face, but it doesn’t because I know they’re fat because I’ve seen them in real life.
R: So, did any of the posts make you feel anything in particular?
Taylor: Just confused, and that’s it, just a bit confused.
R: Were they the videos?
Taylor: Yeah, the videos. There was one about girls fighting and then it turned into Ben10 and it was a bit weird, I didn’t understand it. Yeah, a bit confused.
R: What’s the difference do you think between a post that you do like to look at and a post that maybe you don’t so much?
Taylor: I guess I generally find that I enjoy posts from people that I don’t know more. Like people I know from high school I see their posts and it just bores me. But if it is a person that I haven’t noticed [before] it’s like ‘oh, you’re interesting’, I guess. Just the people in it and whether I know them or not would be the difference of whether I find it interesting or not.
R: Why do you think the posts of people you do know are a bit boring?
Taylor: I guess just because I’ve seen them loads before, it’s a bit like ‘I know what you look like and I know you are going to make yourself look nothing like that in your Instagram posts’ it’s a bit boring. So, just stuff like that.
R: Why do you think people make themselves look different for Instagram?
Taylor: I don’t know, to make them feel like the version they want to be in their head. And then they have this online persona of being able to be that person and getting the ‘likes’ and ‘comments’ that they want, whereas they don’t necessarily get that in real life, so they feel like they are missing out.
R: So, they are missing out on that in real life would you say? So they make up for it online?
Taylor: Yeah, with filters and editing.
R: What do you think of people using editing and filters?
Taylor: Editing I’m not a big fan of unless it’s like sticking a picture or a gif onto it. I think the filters aren’t necessary, I guess like because people that you know are going to see it and they are going to comment like you ‘don’t actually look like that’. You can use filters as long as it doesn’t change the basics of how you look, if it’s a filter that changes the lighting and stuff like that.
R: What impact do you think that using filters that do actually change how you look has on people that see the image?
Taylor: I think the people that see it, it makes them view themselves in a more negative light. Because mostly when you see a picture you don’t think of the editing that goes into it, you just go ‘oh I want to be like her, she’s really skinny or pretty’ and then they have this ideal of what everyone looks like even though they never looked like that in the first place. It just creates this whole negative cycle thing.
R: What sort of posts did you come across while you were browsing?
Taylor: There were a couple of selfies, some of the weird videos that confused me, there were loads of adverts, and then the hair dying and there was a couple of piercing posts. That was about it I think.
R: What are your views on selfie taking?
Taylor: I have no issues with selfies, it was just the selfies that I saw I had issues with. Because I know these people and I know that’s not what they look like in real-life, you’re just playing yourself kind of feeling. Kind of annoyance which sounds really bad out loud. And sometimes they put these filters on and look worse, because then they look fake.
R: So, you said before, people might comment on the use of filters, have you seen this before?
Taylor: Once or twice with people I know, generally more on the browse feature. But then again with the people I know, they delete the comment when they say you don’t look like that. So, it’s only up for like a second and then they delete the comment.
R: Do you think that if you saw an image where someone had used a filter to change the way they looked and you saw a comment that called them out on it, do you think that would affect the way that you feel?
Taylor: Yeah, it would probably make me feel a bit better, because I’d be like ‘okay they don’t actually look like that’. Yeah, it would just make me feel a bit better and change how I viewed the original post.
R: And the person in the post would you say?
Taylor: Yeah.
R: How so?
Taylor: If they had been called out for editing and filtering it massively I would be a bit like, I want to say disgust but it’s not really disgust, like a very low level of disgust, or mild annoyance. It’s like ‘you’re putting this out for everyone else to see. People that know you are going to know it, what’s the point of pretending to people that you don’t know’.

May: I don’t know, you know when people send you memes and you have to follow to see them, I just follow and they are just there on your news feed, so that is just literally what fills my news feed.
R: Do you ever read any of them?
May: Yeah, I read all of them. I don’t know why, they just sort of capture my attention, I read every single one and if they don’t mean anything [to me] then I just don’t think anything and scroll down to the next one.
R: Do you think there is a maximum amount of text on a meme or a text post for one that you would read as opposed to one that you wouldn’t?
May: Yeah, definitely, if there was loads like that first… I’m not going to be able to find it now, but that first one I saw that was about Love Island… I wonder if I can find it, I feel like it’s going to refresh. But it had, it was like that [shows researcher], it had so much text on it and the only thing that really made me read it was the picture of Love Island I could see that and was like ‘oh I watched that last night’ and so that was why I was like ‘okay, I’ll read it because it might be something interesting’. But if it was just that text by itself, lots and lots and just little – I wouldn’t read it.
R: So, you said you got a fair few adverts as well, do you find them quite targeted?
May: Maybe, yeah. I remember when I was buying… I think just before I came back to uni this term, I was trying to find some nice clubbing dresses and so I was going on lots of websites, just on my google, and then I got so many ads just about dresses from websites like Oh! Polly, or anything like Misguided, so many ads. And it will be ads of the exact same dress that I had clicked on just before.
R: Do you have an opinion of targeted ads?
May: It’s not that much effort just to scroll past it. Like, I got one for a Samsung phone and I just didn’t care. Maybe if my phone was really old and I had an ad about the new iPhone maybe I would stop, I don’t think I would ever click on it, but I’d stop and just think about wanting a new phone and then I would probably move on.
R: So, you also mentioned that there was a lingerie company and they had a variety of women, how did that make you feel?
May: Good, it was nice to see both kind of stick thin women and women that were a bit curvier, and like I said they all looked really nice I wasn’t looking at any one of them thinking that I prefer your body. I wasn’t thinking that, I was just thinking that looks really nice.
